title: Google\Cloud\Bigtable\V2\Gapic\BigtableGapicClient
name: BigtableGapicClient
description: Service Description: Service for reading from and writing to existing Bigtable tables.

methods.name: tableName
methods.description: Formats a string containing the fully-qualified path to represent a table resource.

methods.name: parseName
methods.description: Parses a formatted name string and returns an associative array of the components in the name.

params.name: formattedName
params.description: The formatted name string

params.name: template
params.description: Optional name of template to match

returns.description: An associative array from name component IDs to component values.

methods.name: readRows
methods.description: Streams back the contents of all requested rows in key order, optionally applying the same Reader filter to each. Depending on their size, rows and cells may be broken up across multiple responses, but atomicity of each row will still be preserved. See the ReadRowsResponse documentation for details.

params.name: tableName
params.description: Required. The unique name of the table from which to read. Values are of the form projects/<project>/instances/<instance>/tables/<table>.

params.name: optionalArgs
params.description: Optional.

params.name: optionalArgs.appProfileId
params.description: This value specifies routing for replication. If not specified, the "default" application profile will be used.

params.name: optionalArgs.rows
params.description: The row keys and/or ranges to read. If not specified, reads from all rows.

params.name: optionalArgs.filter
params.description: The filter to apply to the contents of the specified row(s). If unset, reads the entirety of each row.

params.name: optionalArgs.rowsLimit
params.description: The read will terminate after committing to N rows' worth of results. The default (zero) is to return all results.

params.name: optionalArgs.timeoutMillis
params.description: Timeout to use for this call.

methods.name: sampleRowKeys
methods.description: Returns a sample of row keys in the table. The returned row keys will delimit contiguous sections of the table of approximately equal size, which can be used to break up the data for distributed tasks like mapreduces.

params.name: tableName
params.description: Required. The unique name of the table from which to sample row keys. Values are of the form projects/<project>/instances/<instance>/tables/<table>.

params.name: optionalArgs
params.description: Optional.

params.name: optionalArgs.appProfileId
params.description: This value specifies routing for replication. If not specified, the "default" application profile will be used.

params.name: optionalArgs.timeoutMillis
params.description: Timeout to use for this call.

methods.name: mutateRow
methods.description: Mutates a row atomically. Cells already present in the row are left unchanged unless explicitly changed by mutation.

params.name: tableName
params.description: Required. The unique name of the table to which the mutation should be applied. Values are of the form projects/<project>/instances/<instance>/tables/<table>.

params.name: rowKey
params.description: Required. The key of the row to which the mutation should be applied.

params.name: mutations
params.description: Required. Changes to be atomically applied to the specified row. Entries are applied in order, meaning that earlier mutations can be masked by later ones. Must contain at least one entry and at most 100000.

methods.name: mutateRows
methods.description: Mutates multiple rows in a batch. Each individual row is mutated atomically as in MutateRow, but the entire batch is not executed atomically.

params.name: tableName
params.description: Required. The unique name of the table to which the mutations should be applied.

params.name: entries
params.description: Required. The row keys and corresponding mutations to be applied in bulk. Each entry is applied as an atomic mutation, but the entries may be applied in arbitrary order (even between entries for the same row). At least one entry must be specified, and in total the entries can contain at most 100000 mutations.

params.name: optionalArgs
params.description: Optional.

params.name: optionalArgs.appProfileId
params.description: This value specifies routing for replication. If not specified, the "default" application profile will be used.

params.name: optionalArgs.timeoutMillis
params.description: Timeout to use for this call.

methods.name: checkAndMutateRow
methods.description: Mutates a row atomically based on the output of a predicate Reader filter.

params.name: tableName
params.description: Required. The unique name of the table to which the conditional mutation should be applied. Values are of the form projects/<project>/instances/<instance>/tables/<table>.

params.name: rowKey
params.description: Required. The key of the row to which the conditional mutation should be applied.

methods.name: readModifyWriteRow
methods.description: Modifies a row atomically on the server. The method reads the latest existing timestamp and value from the specified columns and writes a new entry based on pre-defined read/modify/write rules. The new value for the timestamp is the greater of the existing timestamp or the current server time. The method returns the new contents of all modified cells.

params.name: tableName
params.description: Required. The unique name of the table to which the read/modify/write rules should be applied. Values are of the form projects/<project>/instances/<instance>/tables/<table>.

params.name: rowKey
params.description: Required. The key of the row to which the read/modify/write rules should be applied.

params.name: rules
params.description: Required. Rules specifying how the specified row's contents are to be transformed into writes. Entries are applied in order, meaning that earlier rules will affect the results of later ones.
